chunks: Say: 'Shall I seek a lord other than Allah while He is the Lord of all things? And no soul earns except against itself, nor does a bearer of burden bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about individual accountability and the final return to God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-An'am is foundational for establishing Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (Oneness of Lordship), affirming Allah as the sole sovereign over all creation. It underscores the principle of individual accountability (Mas'uliyyah al-Fardiyyah), rejecting intercessory burden-sharing, and points to the Day of Judgment as the ultimate resolution for theological and jurisprudential differences among humanity.
